messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Canary rollout 'model-v5-quant' (canary pool) reporting p99 latency spike above SLO. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/canary/model-v5-quant
incident-bot: Metrics snapshot: p95=210ms (baseline 45ms), p99=2.1s (baseline 160ms), streaming stall rate +7.2% in last 5m. Affected route: /v1/generate (streaming).

rob: ack. I'm oncall. Paging SREs + runtime. @maya @sophia please join.

maya: looking. Seeing a big tail on websocket worker 7 (host i-0a1b2c). Logs show repeated KV-cache misses and long kernel selection times (~350ms) per init for the new quantized kernels.

sophia: interesting — model-v5-quant changed the kernel selection path and added int8 fallback for some ops. Could be falling back to slow CPU kernels under certain seq len patterns. Pulling traces now.

rob: customer impact?

ella: product-ops: ~2.3% of requests from canary traffic have >1s latency, ~0.6% >3s. No customer-facing pages yet but a few telemetry alerts triggered downstream (ingest backlog).

maya: stack trace sample (excerpt):
```
2026-03-14T02:08:12Z worker-7 model-v5-quant: select_kernel() took 345ms for op matmul_q8 -> fallback to cpu_gemm
2026-03-14T02:08:12Z kvcache: miss prefix 0x7f34, trying disk fetch (120ms)
2026-03-14T02:08:13Z stream: chunk send delay 1200ms, client=eu-west-1
```

rob: that matches the p99. Could be two issues compounding: quantization kernel fallback + kvcache thrash. Any config differences in canary?

sophia: canary config: batch_size=8, max_seq=1024, cache_mode=auto, routing=10% of traffic. The canary model binary is using a different kernel map (opt-level=aggressive). I suspect the aggressive kernel map is misdetecting instruction set on some hosts.

maya: quick mitigation options: 1) shift canary traffic back to 0% (stop), 2) rollback to model-v4 (previous stable), 3) apply hotfix to kernel map (hard). I can do a traffic shift now.

rob: do the traffic shift to 0% first to stop blast radius. Deploy-bot, can you set canary weight=0?

deploy-bot: Command received: set_canary_weight canary-id=model-v5-quant weight=0%. Starting traffic shift. Estimated completion 20s.

deploy-bot: Traffic shift complete. Canary weight=0%.

maya: metrics updating — p95 down to 48ms, p99 trending toward baseline 170ms. Streaming stall rate falling.

ella: documenting customer impact: brief spike at 02:07-02:12 UTC, ~6000 requests affected. No escalations from sales so far.

rob: good. Next: decide permanent action. Options: rollback model bundle from canary to stable, or patch quant kernel map then re-run canary. Which is faster?

sophia: rollback to model-v4 is fastest and safest for customer SLAs. Hotfix requires rebuild + verification and could take hours.

maya: agree. I'll open rollback. rob, do you want me to roll back now?

rob: yes proceed. Keep me posted. Also capture a few more traces for postmortem.

maya: initiating rollback via runway api: 
```
POST /deployments/canary/rollback
{"target_model":"model-v4-stable","reason":"canary p99 spike/kvcache thrash"}
```

deploy-bot: Rollback job queued. Job id: rb-1932109-42. Progress: 0%

deploy-bot: Rollback in progress: draining canary, routing to stable replicas. Progress: 60%.

deploy-bot: Rollback complete. Active model for canary pool: model-v4-stable.

maya: validating — p95=46ms, p99=165ms, streaming stall rate <=0.2%. Good.

rob: nice. Create a short incident ticket and assign to eng-runtime for root cause and mitigations. Tagging @sophia for kernel investigation.

sophia: will own. Initial hypotheses to investigate: kernel autodetect failure on subset of hosts (microcode/driver mismatch), and KV cache access pattern change triggered by different allocation in quantized model. Will reproduce in staging with same seq length distribution.

ella: filing incident doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-19321 — summary + timeline + customer impact. Adding product + support notes.

rob: handoff: I'm oncall for next 9m then handing to night. @oncall-rotating, can you pick this up for follow-up?

oncall-rotating: taking it. I'll coordinate postmortem and any rollout gating.

rob: TL;DR: Canary model-v5-quant caused p99 spike due to kernel fallbacks + kvcache misses. Immediate mitigation: traffic shift to 0% + rollback to model-v4. Customer impact small but tracked. Follow-ups: kernel autodetect fix, add canary preflight checks for kernel map + seq-len tail simulation, tune kvcache warmup during canary. :white_check_mark:

ella: thanks team. I'll notify affected customers with a note: brief degradation, mitigation applied, follow-up postmortem promised.

sophia: adding one more: add an automatic early-stop rule for canaries that hit p99 > 1.0s for >1% of requests in 5m. Should reduce blast radius for future rollouts.

rob: agreed, add to runbook. Closing Slack thread once incident doc is linked.

ella: incident doc linked in ticket. Closing.
